Airplanes with wing tanks can equalize the weight laterally by moving fuel side-to-side, but an improper distribution of weight front/back can make the plane aerodynamically unstable (if the center of gravity is aft of the center of lift), and if it's severe enough it can cause the plane to crash. That is what happened to Air Midwest Flight 5481, killing everyone on board. (there were several contributing factors, but in order of importance: 1) the center of gravity was well behind the center of lift, 2) the plane was overloaded because of fat passengers and too much baggage, 3) the horizontal stabilizer was improperly adjusted and couldn't move far enough to break the stall). Something similar happened to this 747 when the cargo shifted to the rear during takeoff, which caused the nose to pitch upward and induce a stall, at which point it corkscrewed into the ground.
